[[File:DecipherCon 2000 DECIPHERCON banner.jpg|thumb|right|320px|DecipherCon 2000 banner]]
[[File:Doubletree Resort Kissimmee aerial.jpg|thumb|right|320px|The Doubletree Resort, Kissimmee. Photo: USGS.]]
'''DecipherCon 2000''' was Decipher's second company convention, held 5–8 October 2000 at the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, 3011 Maingate Lane, Kissimmee, Florida. It hosted the [[2000 Decipher World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]], in which [[Matt Sokol]] defeated [[Yannick Lapointe]].<ref name="sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (Wayback 9 October 2006)</ref><ref name="jls3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001117011300/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/jls3.html Matt Sokol, 2000 Star Wars CCG World Champion!], Jean-Luc Simard, Decipher (Wayback 17 November 2000)</ref><ref name="addr">[https://www.travelweekly.com/Hotels/Kissimmee-FL/Holiday-Inn-Resort-by-the-Parks-p60120676 Holiday Inn Resort by the Parks], Travel Weekly (3011 Maingate Lane, Kissimmee, FL 34747; telephone 407-396-1400). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026015153/https://swccg.com/snapshots/travelweekly/holiday-inn-resort-by-the-parks-p60120676.html Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''Format:''' various: World Championship [[Premiere - Death Star II]]; side events included [[Death Star II Closed Environment]], [[Reflections Booster Draft]] and [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck (format)|Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]]

The 1999 convention had been in Virginia Beach ([[DecipherCon 1999]]). Decipher billed 2000 as "the Whole Shebang": World Championship play, first looks at new product, and seminars inside product development.<ref name="home">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040217015645/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ DecipherCon 2000], Decipher (Wayback 17 February 2004)</ref><ref name="tfn">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Decipher_Update_DecipherCon_2000_75291.asp Decipher Update: DecipherCon 2000], TheForce.net (5 September 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009010023/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Decipher_Update_DecipherCon_2000_75291.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

== Venue and dates ==

* '''Dates:''' 5–8 October 2000 (Thursday–Sunday)
* '''Site:''' Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, 3011 Maingate Lane, Kissimmee, Florida<ref name="sched" /><ref name="addr" />
* '''Master of ceremonies:''' [[Mark Tuttle]], Decipher net representative<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="insider">Rich Handley, "Deal With It! It's a CCG TKO When Star Wars Fans Compete at DecipherCon 2000", ''Star Wars Insider'' 52, pp. 68–69. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/star-wars-insider-d39bd7/page/n67/mode/2up Internet Archive]. On sale from 27 February 2001: [http://www.starwars.com/community/news/2001/02/news20010221.html Star Wars Insider #52], StarWars.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010418040709/http://www.starwars.com:80/community/news/2001/02/news20010221.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The hotel is two seven-story towers joined by a lobby, about a mile from the Walt Disney World entrance. The same building later operated as Holiday Inn Resort Kissimmee by the Parks.<ref name="addr" />

World Championship constructed days ran Thursday through Saturday. Sunday held the team constructed event and remaining side tournaments.<ref name="sched" /><ref name="events">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081013224103/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/events.html DecipherCon master tournament schedule], Decipher (Wayback 13 October 2008)</ref>

A false fire alarm at 7 a.m. on Friday 6 October emptied the hotel. [[Maarten Logghe]] was in the parking lot when staff called it a false alarm.<ref name="loftus">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050318081253/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/rl1.html FIRE ALARM], Rich Loftus, Decipher (Wayback 18 March 2005)</ref>

== Guests ==

Special guests were [[Michonne Bourriague]] (Aurra Sing) and [[Shannon Baksa]] (Mara Jade). Both sat autograph tables during the weekend.<ref name="home" /><ref name="tfn" />

Saturday 7 October at 1 p.m. [[Tom Lischke]] held a Star Wars CCG question-and-answer session, including the upcoming [[Shadows of the Empire]] expansion. Friday's program included a card-production seminar and a Digital Deck demonstration.<ref name="seminars">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061114195529/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/seminars/ DecipherCon 2000 seminars], Decipher (Wayback 14 November 2006)</ref><ref name="loftus" /><ref name="tfn" />

The first annual Decipher Olympics held sorting competitions, card-house building, and card tosses. One card toss sent a card the length of the hall into a chandelier.<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="hickey">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ mr-hickey-goes-to-florida], Charles "Teacher" Hickey, Decktech (14 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009010025/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

Full results, lists, decks, and the Final Confrontation are on [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]. The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Death Star II]]. [[Justin Pakes]] directed the Star Wars rooms. Sokol (United States) defeated Lapointe (Canada).<ref name="home" /><ref name="jls3" /><ref name="tennet">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cards], Alex "Greedo" Tennet, Decktech (13 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008203411/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Day 1 had 72 players. Sokol finished 36th, then advanced through Day 2 and Day 3. Twelve players reached Day 3. Lapointe led that table 8 (+47). Sokol 6 (+23) took the second Final Confrontation seat.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016121021/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="insider" /><ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010303120030/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars3.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 3], Decipher (Wayback 3 March 2001)</ref><ref name="sokol-trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref>

Day 1 started hours late. Sokol wrote that the open began about 1 p.m., three hours after the posted time.<ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025142704/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[John Arendt]] waited three hours past the published start.<ref name="arendt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2], John Arendt, Decktech (9 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025191728/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Hayes Hunter]] later said first pairings went up at 1 p.m. when play was supposed to start in the morning, and the day ran until 2 a.m.<ref name="hayes-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2794s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 46:34–46:54. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref> [[Charlie Herren]] called Day 1 the most poorly run tournament he had seen.<ref name="herren">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercond1322/ the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercon], Charlie Herren, Decktech (11 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025141130/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercond1322/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Paul Todd Feldman]] said the tournament software was not working properly and that pairings took a long time.<ref name="feldman-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=2428s SWCCG PDS2: Paul Todd Feldman Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025), 40:28–40:37. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive].</ref>

Players' tournament reports also describe events that were not on the printed schedule: [[2000 DecipherCon IRC 8-Man]], [[2000 DecipherCon 8-Man (Friday, Clay Ramey)]], [[2000 DecipherCon 8-Man (Friday, Brian Terwilliger)]], [[2000 DecipherCon 8-Man (Saturday, Charles Hickey)]], [[2000 DecipherCon Squadron Member Secret Squirrel]].

Thursday's first [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] product tournament drew 24 players in a side hall while Worlds Day 1 ran next door. Light Side dominated (Lapointe was the only Dark winner after game 1). [[Koen Meijssen]] (Holland) 8 (+69) beat [[Martin Akesson]] (Sweden) 6 (+17) in the final by 3 Force. [[Jeff Weitkamp]] (Gold 40) was tournament director.<ref name="fkl2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher (Wayback 7 January 2001)</ref>

== Other games ==

The same weekend held World Championships for ''Star Trek'' CCG (Eric Johnfauno over Brian Sykes) and Young Jedi (Ian Vincent over [[Philippe Parise]]), plus more than 60 side tournaments.<ref name="home" /><ref name="insider" /> [[James Monsebroten]], the Bolarus IX Regional champion, placed 12th in the Star Trek final round of 12.<ref name="st00-monsebroten">[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/deckdesigns/111700monsebroten.html Familiar Faces: James Monsebroten, 12th place – 2000 Star Trek CCG World Championships], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010210230841/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/deckdesigns/111700monsebroten.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st00-finalists">[http://www.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/stfinalists.html DecipherCon 2000: Star Trek CCG Qualifiers], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010216105711/http://www.decipher.com:80/tournaments/deciphercon2000/stfinalists.html Internet Archive]</ref> Saturday night's Great Tribble Hunt was a scheduled ''Star Trek'' side event.<ref name="events" /> [[Evan Lorentz]], [[Bill Martinson]] and [[Tim Ellington]] ran the Star Trek CCG Design-a-Card seminar.<ref name="fkl1">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl1.html Design a Card, Any Card], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher, DecipherCon 2000 reports (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010107220600/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl1.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Radio Free Decipher ==

[[Radio Free Decipher]] covered the convention in the weeks around it. On Broadcast 37, [[Kyle Heuer]] and [[Evan Lorentz]] said DecipherCon 2000 would be held in Kissimmee, near Orlando, in October.<ref name="rfd37">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RvBxxX2Tmd4 Broadcast 37 - Radio Free Decipher (09 June, 2000): Joe Boulden, DSII Spoilers, Tribbles, Card Art], Player's Council (YouTube), 0:17–1:00. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-RvBxxX2Tmd4 Internet Archive]</ref>

On Broadcast 50 (15 September 2000), [[Mark Tuttle]], the weekend's master of ceremonies, named three products that would be seen there first: ''Star Trek'' CCG Enhanced Premiere, the [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] and ''Star Trek'' CCG Reflections: The First Five-Year Mission, a set of 100 foil cards. He said the Enhanced Premiere and Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck cards would be legal in the Sunday team tournaments before they were legal anywhere else, and that all three would be on sale in the Decipher store all weekend. Players who pre-registered on the Decipher website would get exclusive Star Wars CCG foils. With more than 60 tournaments, he asked players to arrive about an hour before each start. The Day One events began at 10 a.m. for Star Wars, 10:30 for ''Star Trek'' and 11 for Young Jedi, and a player whose command card was not filled out could be bumped. He said [[Shannon Baksa]] would sign from Thursday and asked fans to bring their Mara Jade cards.<ref name="rfd50">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UhZv7OpkOwA Broadcast 50 - Radio Free Decipher (15 September, 2000): GenCon 2000 Celebrity Interviews], Player's Council (YouTube), 0:06–4:58. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-UhZv7OpkOwA Internet Archive]</ref>

On Broadcast 51 (22 September 2000), Tuttle listed what to pack: best decks and extra cards, spending money for the three new products, items for autographs, and a Trouble with Tribbles deck or boxed game for the Tribbles pit. He described the three Decipher Olympics events: card throwing, card sorting and building a card house. Anyone could enter, with no game experience needed.<ref name="rfd51">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2tQmFqhsx74 Broadcast 51 - Radio Free Decipher (22 September, 2000): DecipherCon, Tom Lischke on Jabba's Sealed], Player's Council (YouTube), 1:53–5:29. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-2tQmFqhsx74 Internet Archive]</ref>

On Broadcast 53 (13 October 2000), Tuttle thanked those who had travelled to Orlando and recalled the Olympics, where the card sorting was by Decipher release date. He said [[Yannick Lapointe]] had vowed to win the championship the next year. Lorentz, who ran the ''Star Trek'' World Championship room, described the Warp Speed tournaments, including one late on Saturday for the 12 ''Star Trek'' finalists. He said Eric Johnfauno and Brian Sykes, both from the Viridian III region, had played a good-spirited final. Heuer had worked on the Digital Deck demonstrations and recalled the Friday night volunteer tournament in Secret Squirrel format. They said Reflections, due out 18 October, had sold out at the convention, including stock moved from the tournament allotment. Jabba the Hutt and the new Lando from Jabba's Palace were played in Sunday's Star Wars team tournament.<ref name="rfd53">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hff_CPT5OY0 Broadcast 53 - Radio Free Decipher (13 October, 2000): Mark Tuttle, DecipherCon 2000 Recap], Player's Council (YouTube), 0:18–7:22 and 14:53–18:06. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Hff_CPT5OY0 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Trip reports ==

Official Decipher "Zoom In" copy came from Francis K. Lalumiere, Jean-Luc Simard, Marcus Sheppard, and John Kaufeld. The Star Wars pieces are Lalumiere's Jabba's Palace Sealed report and Simard's Final Confrontation report.<ref name="reports">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001116233700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/index.html DecipherCon 2000 reports], Decipher (Wayback 16 November 2000)</ref> Rich Loftus wrote the Friday fire-alarm floor report.<ref name="loftus" />

''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' 52 carried [[Richard Handley]]'s report "[[Deal With It! (Star Wars Insider)|Deal With It!]]" on the Star Wars CCG and Young Jedi Knights World Championships, with the guests and the DecipherCon Olympics.<ref name="insider" />

Player reports went up on Decktech within days. They describe the late Day 1 start, deck-check disqualifications, and the Final Confrontation:

* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ Matt Sokol] — all three Worlds days, [[Team Albany]], the missing Luke, and the Final Confrontation
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-world-day-3-whos-the-man-not-med1324/ Yannick Lapointe] — Day 3 table, Super Falcon vs Sokol, and the Final Confrontation
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ Alex Tennet] — UK travel, [[Team OK-UK]] shirts, Day 1 games, DQs, and watching the final
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ Charles Hickey] — Endor crew, card toss, Day 1 games
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercond1322/ Charlie Herren] — Day 1 wait, pickup games, "most poorly run tourney I have ever seen"
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ John Arendt] — three-hour wait past the posted start
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], Trandosite, 25 October 2000 (Rod Latham / Alex Tennet)
* Decktech also carried reports from [[Dominic Gaudreault]], [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Bastian Winkelhaus]], Doug Faust, [[Martin Akesson]], [[Mike Kessling]], Tim Guzman, and others, indexed from [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/tournament_reports/ the tournament-reports list] under 8–15 October 2000

Later interviews returned to the same weekend:
